THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  221

our father was the head of this school, later returned to Florence, Alabama, his native state and there became one of its most distinguished citizens, a member of and leader in the Alabama Constitution Convention of 1901. His service to his people was the culmination of that principle of good government inculcated in his association with, and admiration for, the man you remember and love as Professor Robert Halsell.

    When our father left the great State of Texas and moved to the Indian Territory, that is now a part of the State of Oklahoma, he gave another quarter of a century to a profession he loved. He founded the city of Bryan County— Durant, Oklahoma—and his associates had sent him back to the State Legislature as their representative in that lawmaking body. It was among the duties of Bryan County that he built the first private school in what was then Indian Territory. That school, conducted by him in Oklahoma and later in Texas, carried on as he did work in Texas.

    His life and endeavors in Oklahoma were but an amplification of the work he had done here for the State of people, and in that new commonwealth, as in this one, he builded a reputation second to no man in his time.

    Thus he spent nearly fifty years of his time here on earth in the service of his fellow man. Every minute of it, we who loved him know, was spent in doing good. He was unselfish beyond all measure. He was a man who gave his best at all times, when he was a man of activity. He was busy, just, and cheerful. His life was an endless example of that noble, that inestimable virtue spoken of by old Carlyle, the virtue of work—work done with the whole heart of man.

    You today have dedicated to his memory a beautiful building that will for all time be known as Halsell Memorial Gymnasium. A structure builded by the hands of man to honor his memory will not endure forever; but you have erected a building not made by human hands but eternal and living forever in the hearts of those who knew and talked with him in life, a noble character, a character that endures in the heritage he left his students.

    In behalf of the living members of my father's family, I want to express our deep appreciation for your love and loyalty and the memory of our father, to the citizens of Savoy and to the others who founded Savoy College. We shall never forget your gracious hospitality and the beautiful sacrifices and the great and good work you have done to perpetuate his memory and enliven his ideals.
notes: Continuation of acceptance address by Mrs. Annie Halsell Woodward.
